figure_01: Course observations and chronological validation. (a) Total prokaryotic abundance; shading marks the 31-observation historical holdout. (b) Outer fitting, gap and validation membership, with all three inner folds illustrated for outer fold 1. The final fit uses all 120 development observations. Block widths represent observation counts.
figure_02: Outer chronological evaluation. (a) Each point is one outer fold, averaged over ten seeds for stochastic pipelines. (b) Colored dots are individual seeds averaged over the three folds; black ticks mark their mean and open diamonds mark the mean of the three separately evaluated ensemble RMSEs. Each ensemble averages all ten predictions before scoring.
figure_03: Inner selection diagnostics within the complete development period. Every plotted score averages three seeds and three inner folds. (a) Fixed candidates and checkpoints by parameter count. (b) Training and validation RMSE at the three checkpoints for each family’s selected base configuration. (c) Weight decay, with marker shape indicating dropout. (d) Training versus validation RMSE. The sparse configurations jointly vary several settings.
figure_04: Compression diagnostics from final inner selection. (a) Lowest mean inner RMSE at each latent dimension, after selection among that dimension’s candidates. (b) Reconstruction error versus regression RMSE; AE and DAE points use the best inner Ridge penalty for each base configuration and checkpoint; PCA points show all dimension-penalty candidates. (c) Paired DAE minus AE RMSE for the twelve matched configurations at the prespecified diagnostic checkpoint of 300 epochs and Ridge alpha 10, averaged over the same three seeds and three folds. Negative differences favor denoising. Reconstruction MSE is dimensionless and measured on clean standardized validation inputs.
figure_05: Predictions on the historical holdout. Panels compare direct regression and environmental representation pipelines against identical observations. Neural and random-forest curves are equal-weight averages of ten members; Ridge and PCA predictions are deterministic. Lines connect contemporaneous estimates across sampling occasions.
